name: Explicit Versioned API Contracts
problem: When the interface between two components exists only as code, its shape is discovered by reading the implementation, its changes are unreviewable, and every consumer learns about a breaking change by failing.
forces: Schema languages add a design step before implementation can start.
Contract-first enables parallel development through generated mocks.
A registry is required for versioning and compatibility checking to be automatic rather than social.
solution: All inter-component communication uses explicit contract definitions in a machine-readable schema language — Protobuf, JSON Schema, or OpenAPI. Contracts are registered, versioned, and backward-compatible within a major version. The contract is designed before the implementation and is the primary inter-component documentation.

appliesTo.guidance: Protobuf for high-performance internal RPC; OpenAPI for HTTP/REST exposed externally; all registered in a central schema registry. Enforced by DM-R02.
Contract-first is the precondition for independent deployability under MS-R01.
Every cross-module interaction is governed by an OpenAPI specification or equivalent; undocumented interactions are violations.
The contract is the AsyncAPI event schema; ED-R01 requires strictAsyncApi=true.
Data products express their interface as data contracts — see PAT-0006.

relationships.note: Contract tests verify at build time what the contract asserts.
Published contracts are the only sanctioned path across a data ownership boundary.

enforcedBy.statement: All inter-module communication MUST use explicit contract definitions (Protobuf, JSON Schema, or OpenAPI). Contracts are versioned and backward-compatible.
